say: Welcome to the Pre Sales Agent Framework. It turns the emails, call transcripts and tender documents you get from a customer into confirmed requirements, clarification questions, specialist assessments and a traceable, reviewed estimate. In this tour we follow one real opportunity from start to finish: Larkspur Mutual, an insurer replacing its mainframe claims system.

The sidebar takes you to your Inbox, Opportunities, Knowledge and Admin. Press Control K anywhere to open the command palette: jump to any page, or create a new opportunity, without touching the mouse.

Before the first bid, an administrator prepares the knowledge the agents rely on. Knowledge Sources are your own delivery guides and playbooks, tagged by product and integration type. Here, an insurance claims migration playbook is registered and ready.
Checklists hold the questions you must always ask for a type of integration. Mandatory items become gaps automatically whenever that integration is in scope, so nothing important is forgotten.
The Coverage matrix shows, for every product and integration type, whether you have documentation and checklists, so you can see where gap detection may be weak.
And the Knowledge Graph draws the same picture as a map. Solid lines are documented links, dashed lines show missing coverage, and red rings flag stale or missing material.
To start a bid, choose New Opportunity. You can type the customer, title, products and industry yourself.

Or choose Import from file and drop in the customer's invitation email. The Opportunity Intake Agent reads it and fills in the fields, each one marked From file with the sentence it came from. Check them, set the proposal date, and create. The file becomes your first source.

Every opportunity opens on its Overview. The tiles show confirmed requirements, open gaps, open conflicts and the current estimate. The submission pipeline tracks each stage from sources added to baseline, and Needs you lists the items waiting for your decision, most severe first.
Further down you'll find the submission blockers, recent activity, and the latest agent decision with its reasoning. For Larkspur, all eight stages are complete and version four is the baseline.

On the Sources tab, drop in everything the customer sent: emails, Teams transcripts, Word and PDF documents, notes, or pasted text. Larkspur has eleven sources, including an RFP schedule, an IT email about the mainframe and payments, and two recorded customer answers. Every source is stored unchanged and versioned.
Select a source to open the Inspector. You'll see who added it and when, download the original, and read the extracted text the agents worked from.

The Intake Agent extracts requirements from every source and groups them by category: functional, integration, data, security, non-functional and commercial. Each requirement carries evidence chips that point to the exact sources it came from. Larkspur has eighty-seven, all confirmed.

Open a requirement to see the quoted passage highlighted in its source. From here you can edit, split, merge, reclassify or confirm it. Confirmed requirements are locked; if a later email changes one, you see it as a pending change to accept or reject. Instructions hidden inside customer content are treated as content and never obeyed.

Next, the Clarification Agent looks for what's missing, and mandatory checklist items add gaps of their own. Here is a second opportunity, Aldermoor Health Trust, still in progress: nine open gaps ranked by impact, each with a drafted clarification question you can edit, merge, approve, export and mark as sent.

When the customer replies, paste the answer as a source against the question. The gap is marked answered, and the answer can update related requirements. If one answer also covers other questions, the app suggests those matches for you to confirm.

Some things the customer simply can't know yet, like how much pre-2015 data needs correcting. Those are marked Unknown to the customer and converted into a contingency, priced in hours. Things the customer must decide or provide become conditions. Either way, nothing is silently dropped.

Now start the assessment run. Specialist agents work in parallel: Engineering for feasibility and per-integration effort, the PM Agent for phases and dependencies, and the Security Agent for mandatory controls. Then the Critic checks their coverage and timelines, and the Red Team argues that integrations are harder than they look.

Each agent returns a verdict, such as proceed with conditions, with a confidence level, the effort behind it, and the requirements it relied on. If you disagree, raise a Challenge with new information and the agent reassesses.
All findings land in one table, ranked by severity. Critical findings block submission until someone resolves them, or overrides them with a recorded reason.

The Conflict Agent compares sources and assessments, and flags contradictions: different dates, different volumes, or one agent sizing a requirement the other skipped. Pick a position, give a reason, and resolve.
For Larkspur, all thirty-eight conflicts are resolved, and each resolution records who decided and why.
The Estimating Agent drafts the estimate from the assessments. Every line covers named requirements, with the role mix and effort hours, and you can edit any line in place with a reason.

Submit stays locked while anything is unfinished. The blockers panel lists exactly what's missing: open gaps, assumptions not yet accepted, open conflicts and critical findings, each with a link to fix it.

Larkspur's estimate is twelve thousand and seventy-two hours. The version lifecycle runs from draft, to in review, to approved, to baseline. A review request was sent to a named engineering reviewer, and their approval is recorded right here.
The Assumptions Register lists every condition the estimate depends on, each linked back to the gap it came from, and each accepted by a named person.

Contingencies are shown separately with their hours. Larkspur carries one thousand one hundred and forty hours of contingency, for unknowns like undocumented status codes and late regulator requirements.
Every change creates a new version. Diff against any earlier version to see which lines and assumptions changed, were added or were removed, and how the total moved.
All versions keeps the full history, with the baseline first.
And Export produces the estimate, the assumptions register and the clarification questions as Excel or Word, ready for the proposal.
Reviewers and owners are notified in the Inbox. Review requests and decisions arrive here, so a reviewer can open the estimate, approve it, or send it back with comments.
Once the project is delivered, record actual hours against each estimate line, with a variance cause. Overruns can name the assumption that failed, which feeds the estimate-versus-actual reports.
To import actuals, download the template, fill it in, and upload it. You see a preview, and nothing is saved until you confirm.
And the Trace tab is the append-only audit log of every action, by people and agents alike. Filter by subject, actor or event to follow any number back to its evidence.

Administrators manage the platform under Admin. Users and roles shows each person's roles, which are managed in Auth0: presales engineer, delivery manager, engineering reviewer and platform administrator.
The Catalogue defines the integration types and work packages that checklists, assessments and estimate lines share.
The Agent Registry shows every agent, its version, model and tool permissions. Any tool call an agent isn't allowed to make is blocked and audited.
And Evals runs the agents against reference sets, checking release bars like extraction recall, citation validity and gap recall before a new configuration is accepted.
In Settings, choose a light, dark or system theme, a comfortable or compact density, and turn on single-key shortcuts.

That's the full journey: from a customer's first email, to evidence-backed requirements, answered questions, specialist assessments, and a reviewed, baselined estimate you can trace and measure. Open the user guide for every feature in detail. Thanks for watching.
